explain.say: Here is a surprising idea: saying thank you can make you happier, not just the person you thank. Look at the circle on the board. It starts when you notice something good, like a friend saving you a seat.

explain.say: Meet Hiro. He had a grumpy day where nothing went right. But at bedtime he writes three good things that happened. That is called a gratitude journal. Do you think he will find any?

faq.q: Why does gratitude make you happier?
faq.a: Noticing good things trains your brain to spot them more often, and thanking people makes friendships stronger. Both help you feel better.
asks: Tell me about the You feel happier
Does being grateful make you happier?

faq.a: A notebook where you write down a few good things, big or small, that happened each day or week, like a kind word or a tasty meal.
asks: Tell me about the Three good things

faq.q: How do I notice good things?
faq.a: Slow down and look for small things: a sunny sky, a friend's joke, a hot meal. Asking yourself what went well today helps.
asks: Tell me about the Notice the good

faq.q: What if I cannot think of anything good?
faq.a: Start tiny: I had breakfast, my bed is cosy, a song I like came on. On hard days, even one small thing counts.
asks: I had a bad day, what is good?

faq.q: Is it okay to feel sad even if I am grateful?
faq.a: Yes. Gratitude does not mean pretending everything is fine. You can feel sad and still notice good things.
asks: Do I have to be happy all the time?

facts: In a 2003 study, Robert Emmons and Michael McCullough found that people who kept weekly gratitude lists felt better about their lives than those who listed hassles.
Writing "three good things" each day is a well-known exercise from positive psychology research by Martin Seligman and colleagues.
